note: Omits 'also' (גם): 'I will also do this thing' becomes simply 'I will do it'.
Adds 'the others' as subject of setting up the tabernacle; source does not specify who set it up.
Hebrew 'into the south' rendered as 'from the south', reversing direction
'prostrate at your feet' rendered 'sit at your feet'; singular 'he accepts/bears from your words' made plural 'they carry'
Renders 'did not drive them out' as 'did not take control over them'; the driving out is omitted.
Adds 'he left them' (أبقاهم), which is not in the source.
Adds 'willingly' and object 'it to him' not in the source's 'we will surely give'.
Omits 'gate' (שער): Arabic says entrance of the city, not entrance of the city gate.
Adds 'from city to another'; source says from city, men to cattle.
Reverses final clause to 'you are not guilty'; also renders 'grant them to us' as 'be gentle with them'.
Adds 'the third band' where source says 'one band'.
Says David stood over the Philistines (plural) instead of the Philistine (singular).
Adds interpretation 'as if he saw sin in him,' not in the source.
Adds 'its diameter' (قطرها) for the laver's four cubits, a specification not in the source.
Omits 'the scribe' and recasts 'chief of the army' as commander of the chief's army.
Pronoun shift: 'all his days' (Josiah's) rendered as 'all their days'.
Adds 'so they sent them away' (فأرسلوهم), which is not in the source.
Arabic changes plural 'them/they' to dual 'them two/they two', adding a dual referent not in source.
Adds 'how much more' (فكم بالحري); source says 'even'.
"your darkness" (תָּעֻפָה) is rendered "it flies"; the idea of darkness is lost.
Subject/object reversed: Arabic says 'his step held fast to my foot' instead of 'my foot to his steps'.
Arabic uses conditional 'if my lips speak...' instead of the negated oath 'my lips shall not speak'.
Pronoun/gender changed: Arabic has feminine 'she/it casts him' and 'from her hand' instead of masculine 'he... his hand'.
Adds explanatory 'of heaven' to 'wind,' not in source.
Renders 'will submit to me' as 'flatter me,' changing the predicate/idea.
Adds 'and my sin' (وَذَنْبِي) after 'my sins,' which is not in the source.
Adds clause 'I will sing of your strength' not in source; also 'his steadfast love' rendered 'my mercy'
Reverses recipient: source says heritage given to me, Arabic says given to those who fear your name
Source's question 'Have you brought us into the snare?' rendered as a statement
Passive 'in your name we are called' changed to active 'we call upon your name'.
Proper name 'Gebal' rendered as common noun 'mountains' (جِبَال), losing the place name.
Imperative 'bow down' (הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ) rendered as indicative 'they bow down', losing the command.
Reverses the metaphor: makes the winds his messengers, instead of making his messengers winds
Adds 'الرب' as an extra subject ('the Lord thanks you'), not in the source, distorting the clause.
Second clause omits 'reproves': Arabic has only 'as a father delights in his son', dropping the verb applied to the son.
Arabic omits 'her fortress' and adds 'her multitude' instead.
Hebrew 'if you make his soul a guilt offering' (2ms) changed to 'if he makes himself' (3rd person).
Hebrew 'he was afflicted' rendered as negation 'he was not distressed', reversing the meaning
Adds 'before his face' (أمام وجهه) not in the source, which has only 'before the Chaldeans'.
Reverses subject: Arabic says Jeremiah answered all the men, instead of the men answering Jeremiah.
Last clause rendered 'he will terrify the pasture because of them' instead of 'he will make desolate their dwelling place'.
Source says 'You covered Yourself in anger'; Arabic adds object 'us' (غَطَّيْتَنَا), changing the meaning.
'before their nose' rendered 'to my nose' — changes the possessor from their to my
'Pleading the case for your sisters' rendered as 'judging against your sisters' — direction reversed.
Hebrew 'polished to consume' is rendered 'polished to flash like lightning'; the devouring idea is omitted.
Renders 'I will be sought by the house of Israel' as active 'I ask for the sake of', reversing who requests.
Statement ('Yahweh will pasture them') turned into a rhetorical question ('Will Yahweh pasture them?')
Reverses: 'inhabitants of Samaria tremble' becomes 'they fear the inhabitants of Samaria'; 'tremble' rendered as 'dwell'.
Source is third person 'They turn justice...', Arabic renders as second person 'You who turn...'
The liar's first-person claim 'I will prophesy to you' is changed to third person 'he would say a prophecy'.
Hebrew 'will dispossess her' rendered as 'will possess/rule her' (يملكها), reversing the meaning
Adds 'resembling intoxication' to the trance, an idea not in the source.
Omits 'acceptably' (ευαρεστως) modifying how we serve God.
Adds the verb 'repaired' (أصلح), a predicate not present in the source text.
Omits 'half': 'will not live out half their days' is rendered only as 'will not complete their days'.
Reverses direction: Arabic says the people 'prophesy to them' instead of being the ones prophesied to.
'in three stories' (בַּשְּׁלִשִׁים) rendered as 'in the thirty', losing the three-story idea
Omitted 'for this cause' (kol qobel denah); Arabic begins only with 'at that time'.
